findings.title: callRpc null widening covers required RPC parameters, contradicting its comment and the PR body
findings.evidence: The comment at src/features/quotes/api/shared/rpc.ts:7-8 and the PR body ("callRpc types optional RPC args as nullable") describe optional parameters. Line 9 is `type NullableRpcArgs<Args> = { [Key in keyof Args]: Args[Key] | null };`, which applies to every key. I added a probe at the head: `callRpc("api_delete_archived_job", { p_job_id: null })` and `callRpc("api_delete_archived_jobs", { p_job_ids: null })` both compile with no error, although types.ts:4413 declares `p_job_id: string`. So strictNullChecks gives no protection for required identifiers on destructive SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, which is the client-to-database boundary the PR's Problem section names. With line 9 changed to `{ [Key in keyof Args]: undefined extends Args[Key] ? Args[Key] | null : Args[Key] }`, the whole app (`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json`) has 0 errors and both probes fail with TS2322 "Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'string'". The broad version is unnecessary, and the fix costs nothing. Runtime is unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace rpc.ts:9 with the conditional mapped type above so only optional parameters accept null. It compiles cleanly and matches the comment.

findings.title: The test named 'uses the generic message when no failure detail exists' never reaches the generic message
findings.evidence: At src/features/quotes/archived-parts-delete.test.ts:88-94 the first mocked call returns failures:[{jobId:'a', message:'nope'}], and the test only checks .rejects.toThrow(). Mutant M9, which changes the fallback 'Failed to delete archived parts.' at archived-parts-delete.ts:53, still passes 5/5. The fallback is effectively unreachable, because failures.length>0 guarantees failures[0] exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the test to say it throws the failure's own message and assert that message, or remove the unreachable fallback and the test together.

findings.title: A production non-null assertion has no comment, contrary to the PR's own acceptance claim
findings.evidence: operations-status-client.ts:121 has 'reader = response.body!.getReader();'. The invariant is enforced inside assertUsableResponse at :79-85, but that is a void function, so TypeScript cannot narrow. The body ticks '`!` only where an invariant guarantees it, with a comment'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make assertUsableResponse an assertion function (asserts response is Response & { body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> }) or have it return the body, so the `!` can go.

findings.title: NullableRpcArgs also lets null through for required RPC params, though a narrower type still typechecks
findings.evidence: src/features/quotes/api/shared/rpc.ts:9 maps every key to Args[Key] | null, required ones included, so a future caller can pass null for a required param with no type error. Replacing it with { [Key in keyof Args]: undefined extends Args[Key] ? Args[Key] | null : Args[Key] } gives tsc exit 0 with 0 errors on the merged tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen only optional keys to null, so required RPC params keep rejecting null.
